title: waltcg screen payloads
description: The exact response payload for each of the nine screens (Manual Entry is the ninth: four of the eight game/language combinations have no automated price source). The API serves exactly this; a response that fails validation is a 500, not a warning. Every field here has a named upstream source in contracts/SOURCE_MAP.md -- fields with no reachable source were deleted rather than stubbed, and the deletions are listed at the bottom of that file.

currency.description: ISO code. The UI shows symbol AND code; there is no symbol-only display.

decimal_string.description: A decimal carried as a string. Never a JSON number: binary floats lose cents, and 0.1+0.2 must not become 0.30000000000000004 in a money field.

money.description: No naked money, ever. A monetary value that cannot state its currency and the FX used to reach it is not a monetary value.

fx_rate_used.description: Null ONLY when the amount is already in its native currency and no conversion happened. Null never means 'unknown'.

fx_as_of.description: As-of date of fx_rate_used. Null if and only if fx_rate_used is null.

derived_value.description: Any value the engine computed rather than observed. Carries what it came from and how much to trust it.

value.description: Null means the engine refused or had nothing to compute from. `unavailable_reason` then says which.

source.description: Named upstream source or 'engine:<model>'. Must appear in SOURCE_MAP.md.

sample_size.description: Null means sample size is not a meaningful concept for this value, NOT that it is unknown.

needs_primary_verification.description: True when this value rests on config still sourced from secondary summaries. Grading fees currently do. It propagates: a break-even probability computed with a provisional PSA fee is itself provisional, and the Grading Lab has to be able to say so without the user opening Settings to find out.

assumption_ids.description: Ids of entries in contracts/assumptions.json this value depends on. Drives the UI assumption chip. Empty array means genuinely no assumption, never 'not checked'.

unavailable_reason.description: Why a nullable field is null. The UI renders a designed empty state naming the reason -- never a blank or a zero.

staleness.description: Freshness of ONE value. Carried by every derived_value, never by a screen or a row: a row with a fresh price and a stale population has to say both, and a single row-level object can only say one. The API decides staleness; the UI does not compute it from timestamps.

kind.description: What sort of data this is, which is what sets the threshold -- >24h for price, >7d for population. 'derived' is an engine output whose age is the age of its oldest input.

card_ref.description: Identity only. EN and JP printings are different cards and never share a card_uid -- see contracts/card_uid.md.

artist.description: apitcg.com. The price feeds do not carry it reliably.

grade_rung.description: One rung of the grade ladder. Price sets horizontal extent, population sets weight. Population is Pokemon-only -- see SOURCE_MAP.

grade_ladder.description: The signature element. Ordered raw -> 8 -> 9 -> 10. minItems 1 is deliberate: a card with only a raw price has exactly one rung, and the UI must render 1, 2, 3 and 4 rungs equally well. maxItems 4 because there are four grades -- grade uniqueness and ordering are asserted in tests/test_contract.py, which uniqueItems cannot express.

envelope.description: Every screen response shares this outer shape.

signal_row.description: Headline number differs by play type but always arrives as a derived_value, so heterogeneous rows scan as one list.

suppressed_count.description: Rows withheld for comp sample below minimum. Shown so suppression is visible, never silent.

buy_route.description: landed_cost is null where the venue has no reachable price API -- the link still works, the price does not.

obtainment.description: How this card enters the world. Manually classified: no upstream source publishes this taxonomy.

language_variants.description: Other language printings of the same art. Separate cards, separate prices; never merged in the UI.

price_history_meta.description: Freshness and density of the series. sample_size is the number of points returned; the schema guarantees no cadence and no minimum, because most of the universe has single-digit graded sales per quarter and a guaranteed density could only be met by interpolating prices that were never paid.

condition_read.description: The user's own read. Model B refuses to move off its conservative prior without a complete one.

refusal.description: Non-null when the engine declined. A refusal is a legitimate result and must reach the screen intact.

missing.description: The checklist. Ordered most-actionable first by the engine.

friction_stack.description: Every deduction between gross and net, itemised. A spread whose frictions you cannot see is not a spread.

needs_primary_verification.description: True when any component is priced from unverified config. The components are Money, which carries no provenance of its own, so the stack states it once for the group.

path.description: psa_crossover downside is capped at fees and lockup; crack_resubmit carries full grade risk. Different trades; must not render alike.

buy_cost.description: Landed cost of the buy leg. Without it net_margin_pct has no recomputable denominator and the marketplace fee has no base to be charged on -- the sale price is buy_cost + gross_spread.

trend_excerpt.description: Link plus short paraphrase. Source text is never reproduced in bulk.

sources.description: Which platforms contributed. An array, not named per-platform fields, so adding a platform later is data rather than a schema change.

backfilled_excluded.description: Always true in production. Backfilled sentiment is excluded from every backtest and flagged here so the exclusion is visible.

ledger_entry.description: Immutable at fire time. Never edited; corrections are new rows.

acting_threshold_met.description: False below 50 scored alerts. Do not act with real money until true.

worst_five.description: Permanently visible. Never collapsed, never behind a toggle.

assumption_entry_view.description: Mirror of contracts/assumptions.json for the editable registry screen.

used_by.description: Every figure downstream of this assumption. The inverse of the assumption_ids carried on each derived_value, and asserted against them: a figure citing an assumption that does not list it back is a dependency nobody can see before changing a number.

used_by_count.description: len(used_by). Carried so the chip can render without the list.

usable.description: False when a required field is null and the engine refuses this venue.

score_enabled.description: Ships false. Cannot be enabled until the score beats all three benchmarks out-of-sample after BH correction.

refusal_reason_code.description: Why this input is missing. Grounded in what engine/ev actually emits -- each code corresponds to a Refusal the models raise or a ConfigIncomplete path, so a code can never describe a gap the engine cannot produce.

deep_link.description: Where this gap gets fixed. Null when there is nothing to navigate to -- a structural absence is not a to-do item and must not render as one.

card_uid.description: Set when the fix is card-specific.

assumption_id.description: Set when the gap is a registry entry. Must exist in contracts/assumptions.json -- asserted by tests/test_contract.py, which the schema cannot do across files.

refusal_item.description: One line of the refusal checklist. GOAL D7 and the design brief both require the refusal state to read as a finished, actionable checklist rather than a failure, so a bare string is not enough: the screen needs something to title the row, something to group it by, and somewhere to send the tap.

id.description: Stable identifier for the gap. Where the gap IS a registered assumption this is the assumption id verbatim, so the chip, the registry row and the refusal line are the same thing to the UI. Otherwise it is the engine's own path, e.g. 'fees.marketplaces.ebay.fee_schedule.bands'.

title.description: Human-readable, imperative where fixable. Not a path.

fixable.description: True when supplying a value clears this item. False for a structural absence -- no population source exists for One Piece, and presenting that as a task the user can complete is a lie the checklist would tell every time it renders.

then.description: A price only I can supply is supplied on Manual Entry.

entry_method.description: How the underlying data reached us. Manual rows come from Xianyu, Taobao, Mercari JP and SNKRDUNK typed in by hand; they run through the same engine but age differently and must stay visually distinguishable everywhere they appear. A single observation is never 'mixed' -- that value exists for values computed from several inputs of differing provenance.

manual_venue.description: Where a hand-entered price was seen. No automated source covers any of these.

manual_price_entry.description: One hand-typed observation. Append-only: a correction is a new row citing the one it supersedes, never an edit in place.

as_of.description: The date the price refers to.

observed_at.description: When I typed it in. Never earlier than as_of.

awaiting_entry.description: A card the app cannot price on its own, and why.

screen_manual_entry.description: Four of the eight game/language combinations have no automated price source: One Piece JP and the three Chinese printings. Their prices are typed in from Xianyu, Taobao, Mercari JP and SNKRDUNK, and run through the same engine unchanged.

estimate_basis.description:
Where the GRADE PROBABILITY behind this figure came from. Distinct from entry_method, which says how an observed price reached us -- the two are independent and a Riftbound card typically needs both: a hand-typed price AND a hand-supplied P(10). Collapsing them into one enum would make a market observation I transcribed indistinguishable from a prior I invented, and only one of those has anything behind it.
  population    -- derived from a pop report, shrunk and haircut.
  user_estimate -- I typed the probability. No population source exists for this printing, so there is nothing else to derive it from.
  config_rule   -- from dated crossover rules.
  none          -- this figure rests on no grade probability at all. A break-even threshold is solved from prices and costs alone, which is exactly why it is the trustworthy half of the Grading Lab's gauge.

assumption_usage.description: One figure this assumption feeds. Figures, not card instances: 'used by 6 figures' should answer 'what moves if I change this', and the answer a person can act on is a list of screens and fields, not a count of rows.

field.description: Dotted path within that screen's payload, array indices omitted, e.g. 'rows.headline'.

label.description: What it is called on screen.
